crackedness_criteria.name: Academic Excellence & Rigor
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's academic performance, selectivity of coursework, and intellectual horsepower as evidenced by GPA, standardized scores, honors, and depth of technical curriculum

scoring_guide.high: GPA 3.9+ or top engineering honors (e.g., Tau Beta Pi), exceptionally rigorous technical coursework load, near-perfect standardized test scores (ACT 35+/SAT 1550+), or demonstrated academic awards/distinctions. Pursues advanced coursework beyond standard curriculum.
scoring_guide.medium: GPA 3.5–3.89, solid technical coursework, some academic recognition but not top-tier honors. Standard curriculum with a few standout courses.
scoring_guide.low: GPA below 3.5 or not listed, minimal academic distinction, coursework does not reflect exceptional rigor or intellectual ambition.

crackedness_criteria.name: Research Depth & Impact
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the quality, independence, and real-world impact of research experience — including publications, conference presentations, Google Scholar presence, and lab leadership

scoring_guide.high: Published or submitted papers (peer-reviewed journals or top conferences), Google Scholar profile with citations, first-author or significant contributor credit, research at a top lab with named PI, or research that has been externally recognized. Clear evidence of independent scientific thinking.
scoring_guide.medium: Active research role in a university or industry lab with tangible outputs (poster, preprint, or ongoing project), but no formal publication. Contributes meaningfully to a research agenda without leading it.
scoring_guide.low: Minimal or no research experience, or research listed without clear outputs, contributions, or continuity. Coursework projects listed as 'research.'

crackedness_criteria.name: Technical Skill & Engineering Execution
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures hands-on technical ability across software engineering, AI/ML, data science, or biomedical tools — including the complexity and scale of projects built

scoring_guide.high: Demonstrates mastery of multiple high-relevance technical stacks (e.g., Python, ML frameworks, bioinformatics pipelines, C++). Has built complex, deployed, or open-source projects with real users or measurable outcomes. GitHub or portfolio shows consistent, high-quality output.
scoring_guide.medium: Proficient in core technical tools with evidence of applying them in projects or internships. Projects are functional but limited in scope, scale, or originality. Skills are listed but partially evidenced.
scoring_guide.low: Limited technical skills listed with little project evidence, or skills are generic and not demonstrated through concrete work. No GitHub, portfolio, or project outcomes referenced.

crackedness_criteria.name: Entrepreneurial & Venture Initiative
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's drive to build, launch, or lead ventures — including startups founded, accelerator participation, venture-backed projects, or entrepreneurial extracurriculars

scoring_guide.high: Has founded or co-founded a startup (with traction, funding, or users), participated in a competitive accelerator (e.g., Stanford Climate Ventures, Y Combinator, etc.), or led a venture-oriented project with real-world outcomes. Shows a clear builder mentality.
scoring_guide.medium: Has participated in hackathons, startup competitions, or entrepreneurship clubs with some tangible output. May have explored a startup idea without full launch, or contributed to an early-stage venture in a non-founding role.
scoring_guide.low: No meaningful entrepreneurial activity. Extracurriculars are purely academic or social with no evidence of initiative to build or launch something independently.

crackedness_criteria.name: Leadership & Organizational Impact
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's ability to lead teams, organizations, or initiatives — including club leadership, team management at internships, or founding community efforts

scoring_guide.high: Holds or has held a significant leadership position (president, director, team lead) in a recognized organization, with evidence of growing the organization, managing people, or delivering measurable outcomes under their leadership.
scoring_guide.medium: Active member or officer in clubs/organizations, or led a specific project within a larger team. Leadership is present but scope is limited or impact is not clearly articulated.
scoring_guide.low: No leadership roles listed, or participation is purely as a member with no evidence of initiative or responsibility for others.

crackedness_criteria.name: Industry Experience & Internship Caliber
crackedness_criteria.description: Measures the prestige, relevance, and depth of internship or work experience — including the selectivity of employers and the sophistication of work performed

scoring_guide.high: Internship(s) at top-tier tech, biotech, or healthcare companies (e.g., Google, NVIDIA, top hospitals, leading AI labs), or a research internship at a nationally recognized institution. Work involved meaningful technical or scientific contribution, not just shadowing.
scoring_guide.medium: Internship at a mid-tier company or startup with some relevant technical work. Experience is real but may be limited in scope, prestige, or duration.
scoring_guide.low: No internship experience, or experience is in unrelated fields with no transferable skills relevant to AI, healthcare, or entrepreneurship.

fit_criteria.name: Healthcare Domain Knowledge
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's understanding of and exposure to healthcare systems, clinical workflows, medical data, or biomedical science — the foundation needed to build meaningful healthcare AI

scoring_guide.high: Formal training in biomedical computation, pre-med coursework, clinical research experience, or direct work with EHR/medical imaging/genomics data. Can speak credibly to healthcare pain points, regulatory environment (FDA, HIPAA), or clinical validation. Major or concentration is healthcare-adjacent.
scoring_guide.medium: Some exposure to healthcare through coursework, a project, or a tangential internship, but lacks depth or direct clinical/biomedical experience. Understands the space at a surface level.
scoring_guide.low: No meaningful healthcare exposure. Background is purely in general CS, engineering, or unrelated fields with no evidence of interest in or knowledge of healthcare.

fit_criteria.name: AI/ML Technical Depth for Healthcare Applications
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's specific AI/ML skills and whether they have been applied to healthcare-relevant problems such as diagnostics, drug discovery, clinical NLP, medical imaging, or patient outcome prediction

scoring_guide.high: Has built or researched AI/ML models applied directly to healthcare data (e.g., medical imaging classification, clinical NLP, genomic analysis, drug-target interaction). Familiar with relevant frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) and healthcare-specific data challenges (class imbalance, small datasets, interpretability). Published or presented work in this space is a strong signal.
scoring_guide.medium: Strong general ML/AI skills applied to non-healthcare domains, or healthcare-adjacent AI work (e.g., bioinformatics, general NLP) without direct clinical application. Shows potential to transfer skills but hasn't done so yet.
scoring_guide.low: Limited AI/ML experience overall, or AI skills exist but have never been applied to anything remotely related to healthcare, biology, or life sciences.

fit_criteria.name: Startup & Founder Mindset Alignment
fit_criteria.description: Measures how well the candidate's profile aligns with the founder journey — including comfort with ambiguity, product thinking, user empathy, and the drive to build from zero to one in a high-stakes domain like healthcare

scoring_guide.high: Has founded or seriously explored a startup (ideally in health/bio/tech), participated in accelerators, or demonstrated a pattern of identifying problems and building solutions independently. Shows evidence of talking to users, iterating on ideas, or pitching to investors. Comfortable operating in early-stage, resource-constrained environments.
scoring_guide.medium: Has participated in entrepreneurship programs, hackathons, or case competitions with a healthcare or tech focus. Interested in founding but hasn't yet taken the leap. Shows product curiosity and problem-solving orientation.
scoring_guide.low: No entrepreneurial activity or interest evident. Profile suggests a preference for established institutions (academia, big tech) with no signals of wanting to build a company.

fit_criteria.name: Interdisciplinary Thinking (Bio + CS + Business)
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's ability to bridge multiple disciplines — the hallmark of successful healthcare AI founders who must navigate science, engineering, clinical reality, and business model simultaneously

scoring_guide.high: Formally studying or demonstrably skilled in at least two of: computer science/AI, biomedical science/biology, economics/business, or clinical medicine. Has applied cross-disciplinary thinking in a project or research context (e.g., building a health economics model, combining ML with wet lab data, or designing a clinical trial with a computational component).
scoring_guide.medium: Primarily strong in one discipline with meaningful exposure to a second. For example, a CS major who has taken biology courses and worked on a health project, or a biomed major who has learned to code and applied it to research.
scoring_guide.low: Siloed in a single discipline with no evidence of cross-domain curiosity or application. Unlikely to navigate the complexity of healthcare AI without significant gaps.

fit_criteria.name: Network & Community Engagement in Health/AI Ecosystem
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's existing connections to and engagement with the healthcare AI ecosystem — including relevant clubs, conferences, mentors, or professional communities that signal genuine commitment to the space

scoring_guide.high: Active in Stanford or broader health/AI communities (e.g., Stanford AI in Medicine, BMIR, health-focused accelerators, HLTH, HIMSS, or similar). Has mentors or advisors in healthcare AI. Attended or presented at relevant conferences. LinkedIn shows connections to founders, VCs, or clinicians in the space.
scoring_guide.medium: Some engagement with relevant communities but not deeply embedded. May be a member of a health or AI club without a leadership role, or has attended one relevant event or conference.
scoring_guide.low: No evidence of engagement with healthcare AI communities, events, or networks. Connections appear to be purely academic or in unrelated industries.

fit_criteria.name: Clarity of Healthcare AI Problem Focus
fit_criteria.description: Measures whether the candidate has identified a specific, credible problem in healthcare they care about solving — a key signal of readiness for a VC+Founders dinner where conversations go deep on problem spaces

scoring_guide.high: Resume or profile reveals a consistent thread of work pointing toward a specific healthcare problem (e.g., rare disease diagnosis, mental health triage, clinical documentation burden, drug discovery). The candidate has clearly thought deeply about a problem space and has relevant experience to back it up.
scoring_guide.medium: General interest in healthcare AI is evident but without a focused problem area. Work spans multiple unrelated healthcare topics or is too broad to suggest a specific thesis.
scoring_guide.low: No discernible focus on any healthcare problem. Involvement in healthcare appears opportunistic or incidental rather than driven by genuine problem conviction.

metadata.focus_area: Healthcare AI startup founders and aspiring founders — evaluating both raw talent/achievement and specific alignment with building AI-driven solutions in the healthcare sector
